canonical_question: Why does the text describe dislocation configurations as 'numerous short straight segments' in HSR at 500 °C but 'tangled and tend to form cell substructures'?

question_variants.question: Why does the text describe dislocation configurations as 'numerous short straight segments' in HSR at 500 °C but 'tangled and tend to form cell substructures'?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text explicitly states that numerous short straight segments are tangled and tend to form cell substructures at 500 °C/400 MPa, resolving the apparent contradiction.

answers.answer: At 500 °C/400 MPa, numerous short straight segments are tangled and tend to form cell substructures.
answers.measurement_outcome: Short straight segments are tangled and form cell substructures
answers.mechanism: Dislocation tangling leading to cell substructure formation
evidence_spans: The observed jog configurations are indicative of a dislocation climb process, and thus the stress-assisted dislocation climb controlled by lattice diffusion may be the operative creep mechanism of the present high-entropy alloy in LSR.
Contrary to LSR, creep deformation in HSR exhibits abnormally high stress exponents of 8.9–14 and an average activation energy of 380 kJ mol −1 .
As shown in Figure 6 , obvious dynamic recrystallization occurred in the present CoCrFeNiMn alloy in HSR.

source_evidence_spans: Numerous short straight segments are tangled and tend to form cell substructures at 500 °C/400 MPa ( Figure 7 c).
